clue.text: One of many so-called religious leaders, pure and harmless

definitions.text: One of many so-called religious leaders
definitions.meaning: first meaning: thirteen popes took this name
second meaning: free of sin or guilt
third meaning: doing no harm, inoffensive

explanation.walkthrough: The 'so-called' is literal: many popes have been called Innocent, from Innocent I to Innocent XIII.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone free of guilt and incapable of causing injury, while the papal name was borne by thirteen pontiffs.

clue.text: Arrest European holding guy up in the Big Apple, for instance

indicators.note: the arrest-plus-European pair holds the reversed guy between them

parts.note: to nick someone is British slang for arresting them

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A New York cop picks up a European tourist and a fellow in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the popular alternative label for New York City, an informal epithet rather than its official title.

clue.text: Looking beyond front page of paper when locals start operating

indicators.note: you look past the opening to reach the paper itself, so the paper comes after it

parts.note: the front page is the opening of a newspaper
The Times is the classic British newspaper

explanation.surface: A reader turns past the front page while waiting for the pubs to open.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's regular pub, so the definition is about pub hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensing hours dictate when a pub's doors may open for business; those set hours are the pub's scheduled opening times.

clue.text: After one's upset, expression of disgust — no more!

indicators.note: the disgusted noise comes after the overturned word
in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: one is, so the word one supplies the letters
ugh is the noise of revulsion

explanation.surface: Someone, having been upset, voices disgust and declares they have had their fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this word as an exclamation tells someone to stop because your patience is exhausted.

clue.text: Piece of music encored in histrionic patriotism

indicators.note: the word sits hidden inside histrionic and is then repeated, as an encore, inside patriotism too

parts.note: the four letters run consecutively inside this word, and again inside patriotism

explanation.surface: An overblown patriotic performance gets an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters hide in both histrionic and patriotism, which is why the clue says encored.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a composition written for three players or a contrasting middle section of a minuet.

clue.text: Faithfulness in a key church position

parts.note: taken as written
C is one of the musical keys, A to G
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: A church job demands loyalty in the right position.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness to an original, as in a translation or copy, is precision or exactness of reproduction.

clue.text: Torture, oddly enough, that's constant

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the word torture: first, third, fifth, seventh

parts.note: its first, third, fifth and seventh letters are taken

explanation.surface: Strangely, torture turns out to be a steady presence.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant in the sense of loyal and steadfast; a true friend is a faithful one.

clue.text: Main themes in section of good book grasped by economist

indicators.note: the Bible section is held inside the economist's name

parts.note: John Maynard Keynes, the famous British economist
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: An economist clutches a passage of scripture that sets out his main ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote is the central idea or principle of a speech or policy, so the plural means principal subjects.

clue.text: As source of help, a set of spiritual lessons?

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: A course in religious instruction is offered as somewhere to turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE COURSE, a course of religious education, which is the question mark's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is a means of assistance one can turn to in difficulty, such as legal recourse.

clue.text: Top way to make quick point in court about male

indicators.note: the tennis word goes around the abbreviation for male

parts.words: way to make quick point in court
parts.note: an ace is a serve in tennis that wins the point outright

explanation.surface: A tennis tip about the quickest way for a man to win a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Court is a tennis court, not a law court.

clue.text: New multinational money to encourage skilled operator

parts.note: the euro is shared by many European countries
to urge someone on is to spur them forward

explanation.surface: Fresh international funding is to support a talented practitioner.
explanation.walkthrough: Operator suggests business or telephones; here it is someone who operates on brains.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon performs highly specialised operations, so is literally a skilled operator in theatre.

clue.text: Like work of unacknowledged author, worth testing out

indicators.note: letters put out of their places, sorted into a new order

parts.note: these twelve letters are the fodder to rearrange

explanation.surface: Assessing whether a hidden author's work deserves trying.
explanation.definitionFit: A book composed by a hired writer and published under someone else's name never credits its real writer.

clue.text: Where to get ready for pledge

definitions.meaning: ready is slang for cash, not 'prepared'
a pledge is an item left as security for a loan

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests preparing to take a vow; ready money is cash, handed over against a pawned item.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker's shop lends cash in exchange for goods deposited as security until the loan is repaid.

clue.text: Capital that's minister's responsibility? Not quite

parts.note: a vicar or minister has charge of a parish

explanation.surface: Is the capital a matter for a government minister?
explanation.walkthrough: Minister looks political but is the clerical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Quantity that Richard fatally lacked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sum or total
second meaning, read as two words: Shakespeare's Richard III dies crying 'A horse! my kingdom for a horse!'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words, a horse to ride, which Richard III lacked at Bosworth Field.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a total quantity or sum of something.

clue.text: Kind of phone message nobody hears

definitions.meaning: such a message is written and read, never spoken aloud

explanation.walkthrough: The message is silent because it is typed, not because it goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a written message sent between mobile phones, read on screen rather than listened to.

clue.text: Fellow-player is kind of tame, repeatedly

indicators.note: a kind of the word tame means a rearranged version of its letters

parts.note: the four letters to rearrange
do the same again: a second rearrangement of the same four letters gives the rest

explanation.surface: A colleague in the side turns out somewhat docile, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow member of the same sporting side plays alongside you.

clue.text: Writer of annuals, sort of

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Victorian novelist and poet who wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles
second meaning: ... annuals are garden plants that survive frost

explanation.walkthrough: Annuals look like yearbooks a writer might produce; they are flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy annuals are tough plants sown outdoors, and Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

clue.text: They're not included among singles from hot American groups

parts.note: musical bands

explanation.surface: Hit singles from popular American groups exclude certain acts.
explanation.walkthrough: Singles means unmarried people, not records.
explanation.definitionFit: Married men are by definition no longer single, so they fall outside that category.

clue.text: River starts in tiny trickle, ends in great torrent?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a river of north-east England reaching the sea at Middlesbrough

definitions.text: starts in tiny trickle, ends in great torrent
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the starts of tiny and trickle are two Ts, as are the ends of great and torrent

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a river's journey, but the letter T is spelt tee, and the plural is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees flows from the Pennines to the North Sea at Teesside, and tees spells the plural of the letter T.

clue.text: Vote in English lawsuit for enforcement of payment

indicators.note: the cross is placed inside the English-lawsuit pairing

parts.note: an action is a legal proceeding
a cross on a ballot paper

clue.text: Returned amount of money in a feeling of hostility

parts.note: a sum of money
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Wave article written in newspaper for abnormally gifted hero

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid

clue.text: Course from Spain — a long hop going North

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes
a leap or jump

explanation.surface: A long jump heading northwards from Spain.

clue.text: Part of swami's state, mentally, that's improperly expressed

clue.text: Garment that's fitting in Amritsar, India

clue.text: Bertrand Russell, for example, mostly ahead of his time?

explanation.walkthrough: Bertrand Russell inherited the title of third Earl Russell in 1931.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher held a hereditary peerage, a nobleman ranked above a viscount.

clue.text: Object endlessly, getting too little to eat?

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Someone keeps protesting at being underfed.
explanation.walkthrough: Object looks like a verb, to protest; it is the noun thing.

clue.text: Killer facing charges has to register with old lawyer, finally

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Inclined to absorb a part of elementary education for this?

parts.note: leaning, tilted
